subject: orthopaedics
title: Bone Architecture and Biomechanics

steps.tx: **Cortical bone** forms the dense, compact outer skeletal envelope, accounting for eighty percent of total adult skeletal mass while providing primary structural resistance to mechanical bending and torsion. In contrast, cancellous trabecular bone occupies the metaphysis and epiphysis of long bones and vertebral bodies, comprising twenty percent of skeletal mass. Trabecular bone possesses an eight-fold higher metabolic remodeling turnover rate, arranged in specialized porous interconnecting plates aligned with principal mechanical stress trajectories.
steps.say: Cortical bone makes up eighty percent of skeletal mass, forming a dense compact outer shell that resists bending. Cancellous trabecular bone makes up twenty percent, arranged in porous plates with an eight-fold higher metabolic turnover rate.

steps.tx: **Haversian system** or osteon represents the fundamental microscopic cylindrical structural unit of compact cortical bone, oriented parallel to the longitudinal axis of long bones. Each osteon consists of four to twenty concentric lamellae of calcified matrix encircling a central neurovascular Haversian canal containing capillaries and unmyelinated autonomic nerve fibres. Adjacent Haversian canals are connected obliquely and transversely by Volkmann canals, establishing an interconnected intra-cortical microvascular network.
steps.say: The Haversian system, or osteon, is the cylindrical unit of cortical bone. Concentric lamellae surround a central canal carrying blood vessels and nerves, connected transversely to neighboring osteons by Volkmann canals.

steps.tx: **Extracellular matrix** of bone is a composite material comprising sixty-five percent inorganic mineral and thirty-five percent organic components by dry weight. The inorganic phase is dominated by calcium hydroxyapatite crystals, which confer compressive rigidity and stiffness. The organic phase consists of ninety percent type I collagen fibers, with the remainder composed of osteocalcin, osteopontin, and proteoglycans. Collagen fibrils provide essential tensile strength and flexibility, preventing brittle catastrophic fracture under physiological bending loads.
steps.say: Bone matrix is sixty-five percent mineral and thirty-five percent organic. Calcium hydroxyapatite provides compressive strength and stiffness, while type I collagen provides tensile flexibility to prevent brittle shattering.

right.title: Organic Phase (35%)
points: Ninety percent type I collagen fibrils

steps.tx: **Mechanosensory osteocytes** constitute over ninety percent of all bone cells, residing embedded within mineralized lacunar spaces. Extensive dendritic processes extend through a microscopic network of canaliculi to communicate with adjacent osteocytes and surface osteoblasts via gap junctions. Osteocytes detect interstitial fluid shear stresses generated by mechanical loading, translating physical strains into biochemical signals. In unloaded bone, osteocytes secrete sclerostin, which binds LRP5/6 receptors on osteoblasts to inhibit Wnt-beta-catenin bone formation.
steps.say: Osteocytes make up ninety percent of bone cells, acting as strain sensors inside lacunae. When bone is resting, they release sclerostin to halt bone formation. When bone is mechanically loaded, sclerostin drops, triggering new bone growth.

steps.tx: **Wolff law** dictates that bone tissue continuously adapts its internal architecture and external cortical geometry in direct response to the mechanical forces placed upon it. Under repetitive compressive loading, bone deposition occurs preferentially along principal stress trajectories, accompanied by resorption in unloaded regions. Conversely, prolonged bed rest, spaceflight microgravity, or rigid stress-shielding plate fixation leads to osteoclastic resorption, cortical thinning, and disuse osteopenia.
steps.say: Wolff law states that bone adapts its internal structure to the mechanical loads placed upon it. Compressive stress builds denser bone along lines of force, whereas disuse or rigid metal plates cause stress-shielding bone loss.

steps.tx: **Periosteum** is a vascular fibroelastic membrane covering external bone surfaces, divided into an outer fibrous protective layer and an inner osteogenic cambium layer. The cambium layer contains multipotent mesenchymal osteoprogenitor cells that proliferate and differentiate into osteoblasts during fracture healing, generating rapid external bridging callus. In young children, the periosteum is exceedingly thick, durable, and highly vascular, resisting complete displacement to produce greenstick and buckle (torus) fractures.
steps.say: The periosteum has an outer fibrous layer and an inner cambium layer packed with bone-forming cells. In children, a thick, tough periosteum holds fracture ends together, producing greenstick and buckle fractures.

steps.tx: **Anisotropic biomechanics** describes how bone exhibits vastly different mechanical strength properties depending on the orientation and direction of applied loads. Compact cortical bone is strongest when loaded in compression (ultimate compressive strength approximately 130 to 190 megapascals), intermediate in tension (ultimate tensile strength 100 to 130 megapascals), and weakest when subjected to shear forces (ultimate shear strength 50 to 70 megapascals). This fundamental weakness explains why transverse shearing forces readily induce failure.
steps.say: Bone is anisotropic: it is strongest in compression, intermediate in tension, and weakest in shear. Because bone yields easily to shear, twisting and transverse shearing forces cause fractures at much lower loads.

vis.title: Mechanical Properties of Cortical Bone by Loading Mode
rows: Transverse fractures from direct blunt blows

steps.tx: **Spiral fractures** result directly from pure torsional or rotational loading forces applied across the longitudinal axis of a long bone. Because bone fails in tension along forty-five-degree shear planes, torsional forces produce a clean, continuous helical fracture line that spirals down the diaphysis. In contrast, three-point bending forces generate a transverse fracture with a wedge-shaped butterfly fragment on the compressive side, reflecting combined tension on the convex side and shear on the concave side.
steps.say: A twisting torsional force creates a spiral fracture as bone shears along a forty-five degree angle. A bending force snaps the convex side in tension while crumbling the concave side into a triangular butterfly fragment.
